title: Maurice Benard Reveals the 1 Thing He Loves About Playing Sonny Corinthos
metaDescription: Maurice Benard has played mob boss Sonny Corinthos on General Hospital for over 30 years — and the show still wants fans to root for him.
author: EpisodeLens Staff
altText: Maurice Benard as Sonny Corinthos on General Hospital, the long-running soap opera mob boss character
html:
Maurice Benard has spent more than three decades playing a man who orders murders for a living. And somehow, General Hospital still wants you to cheer for him. That's the strange magic of Sonny Corinthos, the mob boss Benard has embodied since the early 1990s — a character who runs criminal empires yet keeps a loyal fan base that treats him like a hero.

The contradiction isn't lost on Benard. Sonny claims he follows a code, and that code is the whole trick. It's what separates him from the villains who come and go on daytime television. He's a gangster, yes. But he's a gangster with rules, and those rules are what make viewers stick around.

Why Maurice Benard's Sonny Corinthos Still Works After 30 Years

Daytime dramas live and die by their villains. Most of them get written into a corner — they do something unforgivable, and the audience turns on them. Sonny Corinthos has dodged that fate for over 30 years. The reason is simple: he's never been written as a pure bad guy. He's written as a man who believes he's doing the right thing, even when he's clearly not.

That's the code. Sonny doesn't kill for fun. He doesn't betray people for no reason. In his mind, everything he does protects his family and his territory. Whether the audience agrees is a different question. But they understand him, and that understanding is what keeps them invested.

Benard has talked about this dynamic before. He's said Sonny claims he follows a code — and that claim is the character's whole foundation. Without it, Sonny is just another mobster. With it, he's a man the audience can argue about, defend, and occasionally hate. That tension is what makes him last.

The Mob Boss General Hospital Wants You to Root For

Soap operas are built on moral gray areas. Nobody stays purely good or purely evil for long. But Sonny Corinthos takes that idea further than most. He's ordered murders. He's run criminal empires. He's done things that, in real life, would put him away forever. And yet, when he's on screen, the show frames him as the guy you want to win.

That framing is deliberate. General Hospital has spent decades building Sonny as a family man first and a mob boss second. His relationships with his children, his wives, and his closest allies carry as much weight as his criminal dealings. The audience sees him at the dinner table as often as they see him in a warehouse. That balance is what makes him rootable.

It's a tricky line to walk, and not every character manages it. But Sonny has been doing it since the Clinton administration. That longevity says something about both the writing and Benard's performance. He plays Sonny with warmth, which makes the darker moments land harder.

What Maurice Benard Says About Sonny's Code

The code isn't just a plot device. It's the thing Sonny uses to justify himself, both to other characters and to the audience. Benard has described it plainly: Sonny claims he follows a code. That's the line the character draws. Everything he does falls on one side of it or the other, at least in his own mind.

Fans have debated that code for years. Does Sonny actually follow it, or does he bend it whenever it's convenient? The show has never fully answered that question, and that's probably on purpose. Ambiguity keeps the character alive. If Sonny were clearly a hero or clearly a villain, the audience would lose interest. Instead, they keep watching to see which version shows up next.

Benard's performance is a big part of why that ambiguity works. He doesn't play Sonny as a monster. He plays him as a man who believes his own story. That belief is what sells it, even when the actions on screen are hard to defend.

Three Decades of Sonny Corinthos — and Counting

Soap characters rarely last this long. Actors leave, writers change, and audiences move on. Sonny Corinthos has survived all of it. He's been at the center of some of General Hospital's biggest storylines, and he's still a major presence on the canvas today.

That kind of staying power doesn't happen by accident. It comes from a character who can be rewritten, reinterpreted, and argued about without ever losing his core. Sonny's core is that code. As long as he keeps claiming to follow it, the audience will keep watching to see if he actually does.

And that's the real trick of Maurice Benard's Sonny Corinthos. He's a mob boss who's ordered murders and run criminal empires for over 30 years, and General Hospital still wants you to root for him. Whether you do or not is up to you. But you're probably still watching.

What do you think — does Sonny's code actually hold up, or has he broken it too many times to count? Sound off in the comments.
